title: "Modern Difference-in-Differences Estimators"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2

## Motivation

The problems of the two-way fixed effects estimator under staggered adoption motivate alternative approaches
to difference-in-differences that explicitly account for treatment timing.

These modern estimators construct comparisons only between treated and not-yet-treated units,
thereby avoiding the forbidden comparisons embedded in TWFE.

In this chapter, we introduce two influential approaches:

- Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021)
- Sun and Abraham (2021)

## Data Generating Process

We use the same staggered adoption setting as in the previous chapter to highlight the contrast with TWFE.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)

set.seed(123)

n_units <- 90
time_periods <- 1:12

panel <- expand.grid(
  id = 1:n_units,
  time = time_periods
) %>%
  mutate(
    treat_time = case_when(
      id <= 30 ~ 5,
      id <= 60 ~ 8,
      TRUE ~ Inf
    ),
    treated = ifelse(time >= treat_time, 1, 0),
    outcome = 2 + 0.3 * time +
      2 * treated +
      rnorm(n(), sd = 0.7)
  )
```

## Callaway and Sant’Anna (2021)

The estimator proposed by Callaway and Sant’Anna constructs group-time average treatment effects,
comparing treated units only to units that are not yet treated.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(did)

cs_att <- att_gt(
  yname = "outcome",
  tname = "time",
  idname = "id",
  gname = "treat_time",
  data = panel,
  control_group = "notyettreated"
)

summary(cs_att)
```

We can aggregate these group-time effects into an overall average treatment effect.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

agg_cs <- aggte(cs_att, type = "simple")
summary(agg_cs)
```

## Sun and Abraham (2021)

Sun and Abraham propose an interaction-weighted event-study estimator that isolates clean comparisons
between treated and not-yet-treated units.

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(fixest)

sa <- feols(
  outcome ~ sunab(treat_time, time) | id + time,
  data = panel
)

sa
```

## Comparison with TWFE

Unlike the standard TWFE estimator, both approaches explicitly respect treatment timing
and exclude comparisons between already-treated units.

As a result, the estimated treatment effects align with the true data generating process.

## Practical Guidance

- Use TWFE only in canonical two-group, two-period settings.
- In staggered adoption designs, prefer modern DiD estimators.
- Always make treatment timing explicit.

## Conclusion

Modern difference-in-differences estimators resolve the fundamental problems of TWFE
in staggered adoption settings and have become the standard tools in applied work.
